Stir the remaining olive oil with the lemon juice into a dressing.
Arrange the rocket, cucumber and chicken, scatter over the pomegranate seeds, mint and pine nuts, and drizzle with the dressing.

title: Nourish bowl with roasted tofu, sweet potato, kale and peanut dressing
instructions: Cut the sweet potato into 2 cm cubes, and the tofu likewise. Toss both with the rapeseed oil and 4 g of the soy sauce and roast in the oven at 200 °C for 20 minutes.
Strip the kale from the tough stalks and wilt it in a little water for 3 minutes.
Stir the peanut butter with the lime juice and remaining soy sauce into a sauce, adding 1 tbsp water if needed.
Arrange the kale, sweet potato and tofu in a bowl and spoon over the peanut dressing.

title: Low-FODMAP bowl with chicken, rice, carrots and spinach
instructions: Simmer the parboiled rice in 90 ml salted water for 12 minutes and leave to stand.

Slice the carrots and steam for 8 minutes until tender-crisp. Cut the chicken breast into strips and fry in 5 g of the rapeseed oil for 6 minutes until golden and cooked through. Do not use onion or garlic.
Wilt the leaf spinach in the remaining rapeseed oil for 2 minutes only and finish with the lemon juice and parsley.
Arrange the rice, chicken, carrots and spinach in a bowl.

title: DASH barley bowl with salmon, broccoli and herb yoghurt
instructions: Simmer the pearl barley in 160 ml water for 30 minutes until soft, then drain.
Steam the broccoli florets for 6 minutes. Fry the salmon fillet in 3 g of the rapeseed oil for 4 minutes per side until just cooked.
Stir the yoghurt with the parsley, dill, lemon juice and remaining rapeseed oil.
Arrange the barley in a bowl, top with the salmon and broccoli and add the herb yoghurt.

title: Keto bowl with turkey strips, avocado, egg and leaf salad
instructions: Boil the egg for 9 minutes until hard, cool, peel and halve.
Cut the turkey breast into strips and fry in 8 g of the olive oil for 6 minutes until golden.
Slice the avocado and cucumber and wash the leaf salad.
Arrange the salad, turkey, avocado, cucumber and egg in a bowl and drizzle with the remaining olive oil.

title: Volume courgette-ribbon bowl with turkey, cherry tomatoes, pepper, basil and rocket
instructions: Cut the courgette into long, wide ribbons with a peeler.
Cut the turkey breast into strips and fry in 4 g of the olive oil for 6 minutes until golden, then lift out.
Halve the cherry tomatoes and cut the pepper into strips. Wilt the courgette ribbons and pepper in the remaining olive oil for 2 minutes only, so they stay tender-crisp.
Return the turkey, finish with the lemon juice and basil, top with the rocket and serve in a large bowl.

title: Wild rice bowl with duck strips, cherries and roasted savoy cabbage
instructions: Simmer the wild rice in 160 ml salted water for 40 minutes until the grains have burst, then drain.
Cut the skinless duck breast into strips, season with thyme, salt and pepper and fry in 4 g of the rapeseed oil for 5 minutes until brown outside and still slightly pink inside. Lift out.
Cut the savoy cabbage into strips and roast in the remaining rapeseed oil for 6 minutes until the edges are brown. Add the sour cherries and warm them for 1 minute only.
Arrange the wild rice in a bowl and top with the duck, savoy cabbage and cherries.

title: Adzuki and pumpkin bowl with miso and sesame
instructions: Cut the pumpkin into 2 cm cubes and roast in the oven at 200 °C for 20 minutes until soft and caramelised at the edges.
Heat the adzuki beans with the grated ginger and 4 g of the sesame oil for 3 minutes.
Stir the miso with the remaining sesame oil and 1 tbsp hot water until smooth. Cut the spring onion into rings.
Arrange the pumpkin and adzuki in a bowl, drizzle over the miso and scatter with sesame and spring onion.

title: Miso pumpkin soup with ginger, tofu and pumpkin seeds
instructions: Dice the pumpkin and simmer with the grated ginger in 200 ml of the stock for 15 minutes until soft, then blend until smooth.
Pour in the remaining stock, dice the tofu and warm it in the soup for 4 minutes.
Take the pot off the heat, stir the miso smooth in a little of the soup and fold it in, then do not boil again.
Toast the pumpkin seeds in a pan without fat for 2 minutes, scatter over the soup and serve immediately.

title: Roasted parsnip soup with pear, thyme and hazelnuts
instructions: Dice the parsnip and pear, toss with 5 g of the rapeseed oil and the thyme and roast in the oven at 200 °C for 20 minutes.
Simmer the white beans and the roasted cubes with the stock for 8 minutes, then blend until smooth.
Finish with the remaining rapeseed oil. Roughly chop the hazelnuts and toast them without fat for 2 minutes.
Pour the soup into a bowl and serve with the hazelnuts and a few thyme leaves.

title: Cauliflower curry soup with red lentils and yoghurt
instructions: Dice the onion and sweat in the olive oil for 3 minutes, then toast the turmeric and cumin with it for 30 seconds.
Divide the cauliflower into florets, simmer with the lentils and the stock for 20 minutes until soft. Lift out a few florets and blend the rest until smooth.
Season with salt and pepper.
Pour the soup into a bowl, drizzle over the yoghurt and serve with the reserved florets.

title: Celery and apple soup with hazelnuts and thyme
instructions: Cut the celery and apple into pieces and sweat them in the rapeseed oil with the thyme for 5 minutes, without onion.
Add the white beans and the stock, simmer for 15 minutes until soft and blend until smooth.
Roughly chop the hazelnuts and toast them without fat for 2 minutes.
Pour the soup into a bowl and serve with the hazelnuts and thyme leaves.

title: Wild mushroom soup with buckwheat groats and parsley
instructions: Simmer the buckwheat in 100 ml salted water for 12 minutes until the grains are tender, then drain.
Dice the onion, clean and roughly chop the mushrooms. Roast both in the olive oil for 6 minutes until the mushrooms have colour.
Add the stock, simmer for 8 minutes, roughly blend half of the soup and leave the rest chunky.
Spoon the buckwheat into a bowl, pour over the soup and scatter with parsley.

title: Fennel and orange soup with roasted chickpeas
instructions: Cut the fennel and onion into pieces and sweat in 5 g of the olive oil for 6 minutes.
Add the stock and the juice of the orange, simmer for 12 minutes until soft and blend until smooth.
Roast the chickpeas with the remaining olive oil in a pan for 8 minutes until golden.
Pour the soup into a bowl and serve with the roasted chickpeas.

title: Coconut spinach soup with prawns and lime
instructions: Finely grate the ginger and bring it to the boil in a pot with the stock for 3 minutes.
Add the spinach and wilt for 2 minutes, stir in the light coconut milk and blend until smooth.
Poach the prawns in the hot soup for 3 minutes until pink, without overcooking.
Finish with the lime juice and serve immediately.

title: Yellow split-pea soup with mint and wholemeal croutons
instructions: Dice the onion and carrot and sweat in the rapeseed oil for 4 minutes. Add the yellow split peas and the water and simmer for 40 minutes until soft.
Roughly blend the soup and fold in half of the mint.
Cut the wholemeal bread into cubes and toast in a pan without extra fat for 4 minutes until crisp.
Pour the soup into a bowl and serve with the croutons and remaining mint.

title: Star anise chicken soup with pak choi and rice noodles
instructions: Place the chicken breast in the meat stock, add the star anise and ginger and poach at a gentle simmer for 15 minutes. Lift out the meat and shred it into strips.
Soak the rice noodles in hot water for 4 minutes and drain. Cut the pak choi into pieces and the spring onion into rings.
Cook the pak choi in the broth for 3 minutes and remove the star anise.
Place the noodles and chicken in a bowl, pour over the broth and pak choi and serve with the spring onion.

title: Beetroot and ginger soup with light coconut milk and pumpkin seeds
instructions: Dice the onion, cube the beetroot and grate the ginger. Sweat in a pot without extra fat for 4 minutes, adding 2 tbsp of the stock if needed.
Add the remaining stock, simmer for 15 minutes until soft, stir in the light coconut milk and blend until smooth.
Toast the pumpkin seeds without fat for 2 minutes.
Pour the soup into a bowl and serve with the pumpkin seeds.

title: Sopa de ajo with egg, pepper and wholemeal croutons
instructions: Slice the garlic thinly and cut the pepper into strips. Sweat both in the rapeseed oil for 4 minutes, then toast the paprika with them for 30 seconds.
Add the low-sodium vegetable stock and simmer for 8 minutes. Cut the wholemeal bread into cubes and soak them in the soup for 3 minutes to make croutons, lifting some out for serving.
Beat the egg, stir it into the soup off the boil and let it just set for 1 minute.
Pour the soup into a bowl and serve with the reserved croutons.

title: Jerusalem artichoke soup with hazelnut oil and chives
instructions: Dice the onion, Jerusalem artichokes and potatoes and sweat in the olive oil for 5 minutes.
Add the white beans and the stock, simmer for 15 minutes until soft and blend until smooth.
Fold in the hazelnut oil and half of the chives.
Pour the soup into a bowl and serve with the remaining chives.

title: Beef goulash soup with peppers and potatoes
instructions: Cut the beef into 2 cm cubes and dice the onion. Brown both in a pot without extra fat for 6 minutes until the meat has colour.
Toast the paprika and tomato purée with the meat for 1 minute, add the meat stock and simmer for 25 minutes.
Cut the peppers into wedges and the potatoes into cubes, add them and simmer for a further 15 minutes until both are soft.
Season with salt and pepper and serve hot in a deep bowl.

title: Gazpacho verde with cucumber, grapes and almonds
instructions: Roughly dice the cucumber and add half of the grapes and 10 g of the almonds.
Blend cold with the olive oil, lemon juice and parsley until smooth and season with salt and pepper.
Roughly chop the remaining almonds. Halve the remaining grapes.
Pour the gazpacho cold into a bowl and serve with the grapes and almonds.

title: Sweet potato and peanut soup with chilli and lime
instructions: Dice the onion and cube the sweet potato. Sweat without extra fat for 4 minutes, finely chop the chilli and cook it with them for 1 minute.
Add the stock, simmer for 15 minutes until soft, stir in the peanut butter and blend until smooth.
Finish with the lime juice.
Pour the soup hot into a bowl and serve immediately.

title: Warm potato salad with mustard, gherkins and turkey breast
instructions: Cook the potatoes in salted water for 20 minutes, drain, halve or slice them and use them while still warm.
Cut the turkey breast into strips and fry in 3 g of the rapeseed oil for 6 minutes until golden.
Stir the mustard, remaining rapeseed oil and a little gherkin juice into a dressing. Slice the cucumber, cut the red onion into thin rings and slice the gherkins.
Toss the warm potatoes with the dressing, cucumber, onion, gherkins, turkey, lamb's lettuce and chives and serve immediately.

title: Lentil and smoked trout salad with horseradish dressing
instructions: Simmer the lentils in salted water for 20 minutes until soft, then drain and cool.
Stir the yoghurt with the horseradish and lemon juice into a dressing.
Tear the smoked trout into pieces and wash the lamb's lettuce.
Arrange the lentils, lamb's lettuce and trout and spoon over the dressing.

title: Quinoa and kale salad with roasted grapes, walnuts and goat's cheese
instructions: Simmer the quinoa in 90 ml salted water for 15 minutes, leave to stand, then cool.
Roast the grapes in the oven at 200 °C for 10 minutes until they just burst. Toast the walnuts with them for 3 minutes.
Strip the kale from the stalks, shred it finely and rub with 3 g of the olive oil and the lemon juice for 2 minutes until it softens.
Toss the quinoa, kale, grapes and walnuts, crumble over the goat's cheese and serve with the remaining olive oil.

title: Buckwheat salad with roasted beetroot, orange and dill
instructions: Simmer the buckwheat in 100 ml salted water for 12 minutes, then drain and cool.
Dice the beetroot and roast with 4 g of the olive oil in the oven at 200 °C for 20 minutes.
Cut the orange into segments and chop the dill. Stir the remaining olive oil with the lemon juice into a dressing.
Toss the buckwheat, beetroot, chickpeas, orange and dill and fold in the dressing.

title: Roasted broccoli salad with anchovy dressing and egg
instructions: Boil the egg for 9 minutes until hard, cool, peel and quarter.
Divide the broccoli into florets, toss with 5 g of the olive oil and roast in the oven at 200 °C for 15 minutes until the florets are browned at the edges.
Mash the anchovies finely and stir with the remaining olive oil, lemon juice and parsley into a dressing.
Toss the broccoli with the dressing, top with the egg and serve immediately.

title: Fennel, orange and olive salad with roasted salmon
instructions: Rub the salmon fillet with 3 g of the olive oil, salt and pepper and roast in the oven at 200 °C for 12 minutes until just cooked.
Slice the fennel very thinly, cut the orange into segments, halve the olives and chop the dill.
Fold the remaining olive oil into the salad.
Arrange the salad, place the salmon on top and serve with the dill.

title: White asparagus salad with egg, chervil and yoghurt vinaigrette
instructions: Boil the egg for 9 minutes until hard, cool, peel and slice.
Peel the asparagus and cook in salted water for 8 minutes until tender-crisp, drain and cut into diagonal pieces.
Stir the yoghurt with the rapeseed oil, lemon juice and half of the chervil into a vinaigrette.
Arrange the lamb's lettuce and asparagus, top with the egg and remaining chervil and spoon over the vinaigrette.

title: Grilled courgette salad with corn, basil and lemon zest
instructions: Cut the courgette into long slices and fry in 6 g of the olive oil in a grill pan for 6 minutes until they have grill marks.
Heat the corn and chickpeas for 3 minutes, tear the basil and finely grate the lemon zest.
Stir the remaining olive oil with the lemon juice into a dressing.
Arrange the courgette, corn, chickpeas and basil and spoon over the lemon zest and dressing.

title: Green lentil salad with roasted pumpkin, sage and hard cheese
instructions: Simmer the lentils in salted water for 20 minutes until tender-crisp, then drain and cool.
Cut the pumpkin into 2 cm cubes, toss with 4 g of the olive oil and half of the sage and roast in the oven at 200 °C for 20 minutes.
Stir the remaining olive oil with the lemon juice and remaining sage into a dressing. Shave the hard cheese finely.
Toss the lentils and pumpkin, fold in the dressing and top with the hard cheese.

title: Light Waldorf salad with chicken, grapes, yoghurt and walnuts
instructions: Fry the chicken breast in a non-stick pan for 6 minutes per side until cooked through, cool and dice.
Halve the grapes, cut the celery into diagonal slices and roughly chop the walnuts.
Stir the yoghurt with the lemon juice into a dressing.
Toss the lamb's lettuce, chicken, grapes, celery and walnuts with the dressing and serve immediately.

title: Barley salad with roasted mushrooms, thyme and hazelnuts
instructions: Simmer the pearl barley in 180 ml salted water for 30 minutes until soft, then drain and cool.
Slice the mushrooms, toss with 4 g of the olive oil and the thyme and roast in the oven at 200 °C for 15 minutes. Add the hazelnuts for the last 5 minutes.
Stir the remaining olive oil with the lemon juice into a dressing.
Toss the barley, mushrooms, hazelnuts and lamb's lettuce and fold in the dressing.

title: Chicken and edamame salad with sesame-ginger dressing
instructions: Cut the chicken breast into strips and fry in a non-stick pan for 6 minutes until golden and cooked through.
Cook the edamame for 4 minutes. Slice the cucumber and cut the carrot into fine matchsticks.
Finely grate the ginger and stir with the sesame oil, lime juice and soy sauce into a dressing.
Arrange the chicken, edamame, cucumber and carrot and spoon over the dressing and sesame.

title: Lamb and parsley salad with pomegranate, cucumber and bulgur
instructions: Leave the bulgur to swell in 70 ml boiling water for 10 minutes and fluff.
Fry the lamb mince with half of the onion, salt and pepper for 6 minutes until crumbly and cooked through.
Roughly chop the parsley, finely dice the remaining onion and dice the cucumber. Fold the olive oil and lemon juice into the bulgur, parsley, onion and cucumber.
Arrange the parsley bulgur and top with the lamb mince and pomegranate seeds.

title: Meal-prep pasta salad with turkey, peas and herb yoghurt
instructions: Cook the wholemeal pasta in salted water for 9 minutes until al dente, then rinse under cold water. Cook the peas with the pasta for the last 3 minutes and drain.
Dice the turkey breast and fry in a non-stick pan for 6 minutes until golden, then cool.
Stir the yoghurt with the parsley, chives and lemon juice into a herb yoghurt.
Mix the pasta, peas and turkey with the herb yoghurt, pack into a box and eat cold.

title: Spelt salad with roasted peppers, artichokes, olives, capers and herb oil
instructions: Simmer the spelt in 180 ml salted water for 30 minutes until soft, then drain and cool.
Quarter the peppers and roast in the oven at 220 °C for 15 minutes until the skin blisters, then peel and cut into strips.
Halve the artichoke hearts and the olives. Stir the olive oil with the lemon juice and parsley into a herb oil.
Toss the spelt, peppers, artichokes, olives and capers and fold in the herb oil.

title: Savoury cottage cheese and herb muffins with pepper
instructions: Dice the pepper finely and chop the parsley. Beat the eggs and mix with the cottage cheese, oats, pepper, parsley, salt and pepper.
Fill the mixture into 4 ungreased silicone moulds. Bake at 180 °C for 20 minutes until the muffins are set and golden-yellow on top.
Cool in the moulds for 5 minutes, then turn out.
Serve with the lamb's lettuce as a snack.

title: Cheese and chia crackers with cucumber and radish sticks
instructions: Finely grate the hard cheese and grind the almonds. Knead both with the chia seeds, olive oil and 1 tbsp water into a dough.
Roll the dough out 3 mm thin, cut into 8 rectangles and bake at 180 °C for 12 minutes until crisp.
Cut the cucumber and radishes into sticks.
Serve the cooled crackers with the vegetable sticks as a snack.

title: Homemade redcurrant yoghurt ice cream
instructions: Wash the currants, blend 100 g of them until smooth and leave the rest whole.
Stir the purée into the yoghurt until smooth and fold in the whole berries.
Pour into a shallow tub and freeze for 3 hours, stirring vigorously every hour.
Leave to soften for 5 minutes before serving, shape 2 scoops and scatter with the almonds.

title: Homemade hazelnut cocoa ice cream with cocoa nibs
instructions: Stir the hazelnut butter and cocoa into the yoghurt until completely smooth, with no lumps.
Fold in half of the cocoa nibs.
Pour into a shallow tub and freeze for 3 hours, stirring every hour.
Shape 2 scoops and scatter with the remaining cocoa nibs.

title: Homemade mango and lime ice cream with coconut and mint
instructions: Peel the mango, roughly dice the flesh and blend it smooth with the lime juice and light coconut milk.
Fold in 4 g of the coconut flakes and the finely chopped mint.
Pour into a shallow tub and freeze for 3 hours, stirring every hour.
Shape 2 scoops and scatter with the remaining coconut flakes.

title: Homemade peanut and banana nice cream with cocoa
instructions: Slice the banana and freeze for at least 2 hours until solid.
Blend the frozen banana with the silken tofu, peanut butter and cocoa until creamy like soft-serve. No pieces of tofu should remain visible.
Serve immediately as soft-serve or freeze for 30 minutes until firm enough to scoop.
Spoon 1 large scoop or a soft-serve swirl into a bowl and eat immediately.

title: Homemade matcha ice cream with black sesame
instructions: Stir the matcha smooth with 2 tbsp of the milk, then mix with the yoghurt and the remaining milk.
Fold in half of the sesame seeds.
Pour into a shallow tub and freeze for 3 hours, stirring every hour.
Shape 2 scoops and scatter with the remaining sesame.

title: Homemade buttermilk and lemon ice cream with thyme
instructions: Stir the buttermilk, yoghurt and lemon juice until smooth. Finely chop half of the thyme and fold it in.
Pour into a shallow tub and freeze for 3 hours, stirring every hour.
Leave to soften for 5 minutes before serving and shape 2 scoops.
Scatter with the remaining thyme leaves and eat immediately.

title: Homemade avocado and lime ice cream
instructions: Stone the avocado and blend the flesh with the lime juice and yoghurt until the mixture is deep green and completely smooth.
Pour into a shallow tub and freeze for 3 hours, stirring every hour.
Leave to soften for 5 minutes before serving.
Shape 2 scoops and eat immediately.

title: Homemade blackberry skyr ice cream
instructions: Blend 100 g of the blackberries until smooth and leave the rest whole.
Fold the purée into the skyr and fold in the whole berries.
Pour into a shallow tub and freeze for 3 hours, stirring every hour.
Shape 2 scoops and serve immediately.

title: Stracciatella quark ice cream with 85 percent chocolate
instructions: Stir the quark with the milk until smooth.
Finely chop the chocolate or grate it into fine shards and fold them in.
Pour into a shallow tub and freeze for 3 hours, stirring every hour.
Shape 2 scoops so the chocolate shards are visible and eat immediately.

title: Baked banana with cinnamon and yoghurt ice cream
instructions: Spoon the yoghurt into a shallow tub and freeze for at least 2 hours, stirring once, until it is firm enough to scoop.
Halve the banana lengthways in its skin, dust with cinnamon and bake at 200 °C for 12 minutes until soft and caramelised at the edges. The skin is only a baking vessel and is not eaten.
Roughly chop the almonds and toast them without fat for 3 minutes.
Serve the warm baked banana immediately with 1 scoop of yoghurt ice cream and the almonds.

title: Coffee granita with foamed almond milk
instructions: Stir the espresso with 12 g sugar until dissolved and cool for 10 minutes.
Pour the mixture into a shallow tub and freeze for 3 hours, scraping with a fork every 30 minutes until a coarse granita forms.
Foam the almond drink with the almond butter for 1 minute.
Spoon the granita into a glass and top with the foamed almond milk.

title: Blood-orange granita with olive oil and sea salt
instructions: Juice the blood oranges and chill the juice for 10 minutes.
Pour the juice into a shallow tub and freeze for 3 hours, scraping with a fork every 30 minutes.
Spoon the granita into a bowl, drizzle with 10 g olive oil and sprinkle with 0.3 g sea salt.

title: Frozen skyr bites with cocoa and raspberries
instructions: Stir the skyr with the cocoa, vanilla and lemon zest until smooth. Roughly crush the raspberries and fold them in.
Spoon the mixture into 8 small bites on a board lined with baking paper.
Sprinkle the bites with 5 g desiccated coconut and freeze for 2 hours until firm.
Serve frozen as a dessert.

title: Passion-fruit sorbet with coconut chips
instructions: Halve the passion fruit and scoop out the pulp with the seeds. Cut the banana into pieces.
Blend the pulp, banana, 8 g sugar and 40 ml water until smooth.
Pour into a shallow tub and freeze for 3 hours, stirring vigorously every hour.
Shape 2 scoops and scatter with 15 g coconut chips.

title: Apple-cinnamon sorbet with toasted oats
instructions: Core and roughly chop the apple, steam with 40 ml water and the cinnamon for 8 minutes until soft, then puree and cool.
Toast the oats in a non-stick pan for 3 minutes until golden, then set aside.
Freeze the apple puree for 3 hours, stirring every hour.
Shape 2 scoops and scatter with the toasted oats.

title: Tofu chocolate mousse with sour cherries
instructions: Crumble the tofu and blend with the cocoa and almond butter for 1 minute until creamy.
Drain the sour cherries, roughly crush 60 g and fold into the mousse, keeping the remaining 20 g for garnish.
Spoon the mousse into a bowl and chill for 20 minutes.
Serve with the remaining sour cherries.

title: Baked apple with oat-nut streusel and vanilla yoghurt
instructions: Cut the top off the apple, remove the core and keep the lid.
Mix the oats and walnuts with the cinnamon, fill the apple and replace the lid.
Bake at 180 °C for 20 minutes until the apple is soft.
Stir the yoghurt with the vanilla and serve with the baked apple.

title: Pears poached in rooibos with vanilla quark
instructions: Peel the pears, halve them and remove the cores.
Poach the pears in the hot rooibos tea over a low heat for 15 minutes until soft, then lift out.
Stir the quark with the vanilla until smooth.
Serve the poached pears with the vanilla quark.

title: Oven-roasted plums with cardamom yoghurt and pistachios
instructions: Halve and stone the plums.
Toss the halves with 5 g olive oil, spread on a tray and roast at 200 °C for 15 minutes until soft and lightly caramelised at the edges.
Stir the yoghurt with the cardamom and roughly chop the pistachios.
Serve the roasted plums with the cardamom yoghurt and pistachios.

title: Espresso chia pudding with almond butter and cacao nibs
instructions: Stir the chia seeds with the espresso and almond drink, leave to swell for 10 minutes, then stir again.
Chill for at least 2 hours until the pudding is set.
Top with 30 g almond butter and 5 g cacao nibs.

title: Espresso quark cup with cocoa and roasted almonds
instructions: Toast the almonds in a non-stick pan for 3 minutes, then chop them roughly.
Stir the quark with the espresso and cocoa until smooth.
Spoon the mixture into a glass and scatter with the roasted almonds.

title: Berry cobbler with oat streusel and skyr
instructions: Put the berries and lemon juice into a small ovenproof dish.
Rub the oats with 5 g rapeseed oil into a streusel and scatter over the berries.
Bake at 180 °C for 20 minutes until the streusel is golden and the berries are juicy.
Cool for 5 minutes and serve with the skyr.

title: Cheesecake in a glass with strawberries
instructions: Toast the oats in a non-stick pan for 3 minutes, then press them into a glass.
Stir the quark, light cream cheese and lemon juice until smooth and spoon onto the oats.
Slice the strawberries and arrange them on top. Chill for 20 minutes.

title: Carrot cake slice with walnuts and yoghurt glaze
instructions: Finely grate the carrot and roughly chop the walnuts. Beat the egg.
Mix the carrot, walnuts, egg, wholemeal flour, 10 g rapeseed oil and 10 g sugar.
Fill the batter into a small tin and bake at 180 °C for 25 minutes until set and golden. Cool for 10 minutes.
Spread the yoghurt as a glaze over the slice and serve.

title: Black-bean brownies with raspberries
instructions: Blend the black beans and dates until smooth. Stir in the cocoa, oats and walnuts.
Spread the mixture in a small ungreased tin and press in 40 g of the raspberries.
Bake at 180 °C for 20 minutes until the top is set. Cool for 10 minutes and cut into 2 pieces.
Serve with the remaining 20 g raspberries.

title: Date and cocoa truffles with sesame
instructions: Stone the dates and blend with the almond butter and cocoa into a sticky mixture.
Shape the mixture into 6 balls.
Toast the sesame in a non-stick pan for 2 minutes and roll the balls in it.
Chill for 20 minutes, then eat as a snack.

title: Meal-prep protein oat bars with cocoa and hazelnut
instructions: Roughly chop the hazelnuts. Knead the oats, whey protein, cocoa, hazelnuts and skyr into a dough.
Press the dough 1.5 cm thick into a small tin.
Bake at 170 °C for 15 minutes until the top is dry and firm. Cool completely.
Cut into 2 bars and eat cold as meal-prep.

title: Lactose-free kiwi coconut chia pudding
instructions: Stir the chia seeds with the coconut milk and almond drink, leave to swell for 10 minutes, then stir again.
Chill for at least 2 hours until the pudding is set.
Peel the kiwi and cut it into slices.
Top the pudding with the kiwi and 8 g coconut flakes.

title: Baked fig tartlet with almonds and yoghurt
instructions: Line a small tartlet tin with the filo pastry, roughly chop the almonds and scatter half of them over the pastry.
Halve the figs and lay them on the pastry, then scatter the remaining almonds on top.
Bake at 190 °C for 12 minutes until the pastry is golden and the figs are soft.
Cool for 5 minutes and serve with the yoghurt.

title: Orange polenta slices with olive oil and pistachios
instructions: Bring 160 ml water to the boil, rain in the polenta while stirring and cook for 8 minutes until thick. Take off the heat.
Stir in the orange juice and 8 g sugar, pour into a small tin, leave to set for 20 minutes, then cut into 2 slices.
Roughly chop the pistachios.
Drizzle the slices with 10 g olive oil and scatter with the pistachios.

title: Kale and pineapple smoothie with ginger and pea protein
instructions: Wash the kale and remove the tough stems. Cut the pineapple into pieces and slice the ginger.
Blend everything with the pea protein and soy drink for 45 seconds until creamy.
Drink immediately as breakfast.

title: Beetroot and berry smoothie with yoghurt and flaxseed
instructions: Peel and dice the beetroot. Grind the flaxseed freshly.
Blend the beetroot, berries, yoghurt, flaxseed and 80 ml water for 45 seconds until creamy.
Drink immediately.

title: Espresso date protein shake with oat drink and cocoa
instructions: Stone the dates.
Blend the espresso, dates, oat drink, cocoa and whey protein for 45 seconds until creamy.
Drink immediately.

title: Papaya and pineapple smoothie with coconut yoghurt
instructions: Peel the papaya and pineapple and cut them into pieces.
Blend with the coconut yoghurt for 45 seconds until creamy.
Drink immediately.

title: Cucumber and kiwi smoothie with lime and hemp seeds
instructions: Peel the cucumber and kiwi and cut them into pieces.
Blend with the lime juice, hemp seeds and almond drink for 45 seconds until creamy.
Drink immediately.

title: Strawberry buttermilk shake with oats
instructions: Hull the strawberries.
Blend the strawberries, buttermilk and oats for 45 seconds until creamy.
Drink immediately.

title: Apricot and orange smoothie with carrot and yoghurt
instructions: Stone the apricots, segment the orange, peel and roughly chop the carrot.
Blend with the yoghurt for 45 seconds until creamy.
Drink immediately.

title: Chai pear protein shake with skyr and cardamom
instructions: Core the pear and cut it into pieces.
Blend the pear, skyr, oat drink and the spices for 45 seconds until creamy.
Drink immediately.

title: Blueberry oat smoothie bowl with granola and pumpkin seeds
instructions: Toast 15 g of the oats in a non-stick pan for 3 minutes until golden; this is the granola.
Blend the blueberries, the remaining 20 g oats, the yoghurt and 60 ml water for 45 seconds until thick.
Spoon into a bowl and top with the granola and pumpkin seeds.

title: Kiwi and spinach smoothie bowl with granola and coconut flakes
instructions: Toast 15 g of the oats in a non-stick pan for 3 minutes until golden.
Peel the kiwi and blend with the spinach, the remaining 15 g oats and the soy drink for 45 seconds until thick.
Spoon into a bowl and top with the toasted oats and coconut flakes.

title: Cherry cocoa protein smoothie with almonds and espresso
instructions: Stone the cherries and roughly chop the almonds.
Blend the cherries, skyr, cocoa, vanilla, cinnamon and 30 ml espresso for 45 seconds until creamy.
Scatter with the chopped almonds and drink immediately.

title: Golden milk shake with banana, turmeric and oats
instructions: Cut the banana into pieces.
Blend the banana, oats, oat drink, turmeric and cinnamon for 45 seconds until creamy.
Drink immediately.

title: Savoury mint lassi with cucumber
instructions: Roughly chop the cucumber and pick the mint leaves.
Blend the yoghurt, cucumber, mint, cumin and 0.2 g sea salt for 30 seconds until creamy.
Drink immediately as a savoury snack.

title: Kefir and plum smoothie with cinnamon and oats
instructions: Stone the plums.
Blend the kefir, plums, oats and cinnamon for 45 seconds until creamy.
Drink immediately.

title: Cocoa date smoothie with tofu and almond drink
instructions: Stone the dates and crumble the tofu.
Blend the tofu, dates, cocoa and almond drink for 45 seconds until very creamy.
Drink immediately.

title: Smoked tofu steak with pea puree and lemon
instructions: Pat the smoked tofu dry and cut into 2 flat steaks. Fry in 8 g rapeseed oil in a non-stick pan for 4 minutes per side until crisp.
Cook the peas for 5 minutes, then mash with half of the lemon juice and the parsley into a coarse puree.
Spoon the pea puree onto a plate, lay the tofu steaks on top and drizzle with the remaining lemon juice.

title: Seitan sauerbraten with red cabbage and bread dumplings
instructions: Dice the wholemeal bread, knead with the soy drink and parsley, shape into 3 bread dumplings and poach in salted water for 12 minutes.
Dice the onion, fry in 8 g rapeseed oil for 3 minutes, add sliced seitan, pour in 40 ml alcohol-free red wine and 80 ml vegetable stock and braise for 10 minutes.
Shred the red cabbage and stew in a second pan for 8 minutes until soft.
Serve the seitan with its sauce, the red cabbage and the bread dumplings.

title: Tempeh ragu with pappardelle and herbs
instructions: Cook the pappardelle in salted water for 9 minutes until al dente, reserve 2 tbsp of the cooking water and drain.
Dice the onion and garlic and crumble the tempeh. Fry in 8 g rapeseed oil for 6 minutes until crumbly.
Add the passata and herbs and simmer for 8 minutes.
Fold the pappardelle and 2 tbsp cooking water into the ragu and serve immediately.

title: Jackfruit barbecue sandwich with bean slaw in a wholemeal roll
instructions: Shred the jackfruit by hand. Mix the tomato paste, maple syrup, apple cider vinegar and paprika and fold into the jackfruit.
Fry in 8 g rapeseed oil in a non-stick pan for 8 minutes until the edges are lightly caramelised.
Shred the white cabbage finely and toss with the white beans into a slaw.
Split the wholemeal roll and fill with the jackfruit and the bean slaw.

title: Sofritas burrito with tofu, beans, salsa and salad
instructions: Crumble the tofu. Dice the onion. Dice the tomato.
Fry the tofu and onion with the cumin and paprika in 8 g rapeseed oil for 8 minutes until crumbly.
Heat the black beans for 2 minutes. Mix the tomato with the lime juice into a salsa.
Fill the wholemeal wrap with the tofu, beans, salsa and lettuce and roll it up tightly.

title: Lentil and walnut roast with tomato glaze and green beans
instructions: Simmer the lentils in 250 ml water for 20 minutes until soft, then drain. Roughly chop the walnuts and dice the onion.
Knead the lentils, walnuts, onion and 4 g rapeseed oil, shape into a loaf and bake at 180 °C for 20 minutes.
Stir the tomato paste with 1 tbsp water into a glaze and brush it onto the roast for the last 5 minutes. Cook the green beans in 4 g rapeseed oil for 8 minutes.
Slice the roast and serve with the beans and parsley.

title: Edamame mint spaghetti with lemon and chilli
instructions: Cook the wholemeal spaghetti in salted water for 9 minutes until al dente, then drain. Cook the edamame for 4 minutes if still raw, otherwise just heat them.
Finely slice the chilli and pick the mint. Sweat in 8 g olive oil for 1 minute.
Toss the spaghetti, edamame, lemon juice, chilli and mint and serve immediately.

title: Besan chilla (chickpea pancakes) with spinach and tomato chutney
instructions: Stir the chickpea flour with 140 ml water, cumin and turmeric into a smooth batter and leave to swell for 5 minutes. Roughly chop the spinach and fold it in.
In 10 g rapeseed oil in a non-stick pan, cook 3 thin chillas for 3 minutes per side until golden and set.
Finely dice the tomato and onion and stew for 3 minutes into a coarse chutney.
Serve the chillas with the tomato chutney as breakfast.

title: Tempeh katsu with cabbage slaw and rice
instructions: Simmer the brown rice in 135 ml water for 20 minutes and leave to swell.
Cut the tempeh into 4 flat slices, dip in the soy sauce and press into the panko.
Brush the slices with 10 g rapeseed oil and bake in an air fryer or oven at 200 °C for 10 minutes until crisp, turning once.
Shred the white cabbage finely. Arrange the rice, katsu and slaw.

title: Kung pao tofu with celery, cashews and brown rice
instructions: Simmer the brown rice in 135 ml water for 20 minutes. Cut the tofu into 2 cm cubes and the celery into diagonal pieces.
Fry the tofu in 5 g rapeseed oil for 6 minutes until golden, then lift out.
Fry the celery, chilli and cashews in 5 g sesame oil for 3 minutes, add the tofu and soy sauce and toss for 2 minutes.
Serve with the brown rice.

title: Lupin stroganoff with mushrooms and buckwheat
instructions: Simmer the buckwheat in 125 ml water for 15 minutes and leave to swell.
Dice the onion and slice the mushrooms. Fry in 8 g rapeseed oil for 6 minutes.
Add the lupins and oat cuisine, simmer for 5 minutes until creamy and stir in the parsley.
Serve the stroganoff on the buckwheat.

title: Lupin medallions with herb sauce and roasted vegetables
instructions: Stir the lupin meal with 40 ml water into a mouldable dough and shape 4 medallions.
Cut the pepper and courgette into wedges, toss with 4 g rapeseed oil and roast at 200 °C for 20 minutes.
Fry the medallions in 4 g rapeseed oil for 4 minutes per side until golden.
Stir the soy yoghurt with the parsley and chives into a herb sauce and serve everything together.

title: Conchiglioni with tofu ricotta, spinach and tomato sauce
instructions: Cook the conchiglioni in salted water for 10 minutes until al dente, then drain.
Crumble the tofu and blend with the lemon juice and nutmeg into a ricotta-like mixture, briefly blanch the spinach, squeeze it dry and fold it in.
Fill the shells with the tofu ricotta. Heat the passata for 5 minutes and stir in the remaining rapeseed oil.
Arrange the filled conchiglioni on the tomato sauce.

title: Vegan buckwheat pancakes with apple compote and cinnamon
instructions: Stir the buckwheat flour with the soy drink and 1 g cinnamon into a smooth batter and leave to swell for 5 minutes.
In 6 g rapeseed oil in a non-stick pan, cook 3 thin pancakes for 3 minutes per side.
Dice the apple and stew with 1 g cinnamon and 2 tbsp water for 6 minutes into a coarse compote.
Serve the pancakes with the apple compote as breakfast.

title: Smoky tempeh and kale stew with white beans
instructions: Cube the tempeh, slice the onion and cut the kale into large pieces.
Fry the tempeh and onion in 8 g rapeseed oil for 5 minutes, then add the smoked paprika.
Add the kale, white beans and 150 ml vegetable stock and simmer for 12 minutes until the kale is tender.
Serve hot as a stew.

title: Udon with crisp tofu, mushrooms and pak choi
instructions: Cook the udon according to the pack for 8 minutes, then drain. Cut the tofu into 2 cm cubes, slice the mushrooms and halve the pak choi lengthways.
Fry the tofu in 6 g rapeseed oil for 6 minutes until crisp and golden, then lift out.
Fry the mushrooms and pak choi in 5 g sesame oil for 4 minutes, add the soy sauce and udon and toss for 1 minute.
Top with the crisp tofu and serve immediately.

title: Peppers stuffed with quinoa and black beans
instructions: Simmer the quinoa in 150 ml water for 15 minutes and leave to swell. Halve the peppers and remove the seeds.
Dice the onion and tomato, fry in 8 g rapeseed oil for 3 minutes, then fold in the quinoa, black beans and spices.
Fill the pepper halves and bake at 190 °C for 20 minutes until soft.
Serve hot as a main.

title: Hummus bowl with roasted vegetables and baked tofu
instructions: Cut the tofu into 2 cm cubes and the pepper, courgette and carrot into wedges. Toss with 8 g olive oil.
Roast everything in the oven at 200 °C for 20 minutes until the tofu is golden and the vegetables are soft.
Spread the hummus in a bowl, top with the roasted vegetables and tofu and drizzle with the lemon juice.

title: Miso pointed cabbage with tofu, soba and sesame
instructions: Cook the soba noodles in salted water for 5 minutes, then drain. Cut the pointed cabbage into wedges and the tofu into 2 cm cubes.
Fry the tofu in 5 g sesame oil for 5 minutes until golden, then lift out. Roast the pointed cabbage in the same pan for 6 minutes.
Loosen the miso with 3 tbsp hot water, pour over the cabbage and tofu and toss for 2 minutes.
Add the soba and scatter with 8 g sesame.

title: Jackfruit tacos with red cabbage, black beans, coriander and lime
instructions: Shred the jackfruit and fry in 12 g rapeseed oil for 8 minutes until the edges are lightly toasted.
Heat the black beans for 3 minutes. Shred the red cabbage finely.
Warm the corn tortillas in a dry pan for 30 seconds per side.
Fill the tortillas with jackfruit, beans, red cabbage and coriander and squeeze over the lime juice.

title: Chicken with carrots, courgette and rice noodles in a lime and coriander sauce
instructions: Soak the rice noodles in hot water for 5 minutes according to the pack, then drain. Cut the chicken breast into strips, the carrot into slices and the courgette into half-moons.
Fry the chicken in 8 g rapeseed oil for 6 minutes until golden and cooked through, then lift out.
Fry the carrot and courgette for 5 minutes, finely grate the ginger and cook it with them for 1 minute.
Return the chicken and rice noodles, fold in the lime juice and coriander and serve immediately. No onion, no garlic.

title: Cod with potato and spinach mash and lemon
instructions: Peel the potatoes, cut into pieces and boil for 15 minutes until soft, then drain.
Wilt the spinach for 2 minutes, then mash with the potatoes, 40 ml lactose-free milk and 8 g olive oil into a coarse mash.
Fry the cod in a non-stick pan for 4 minutes per side until cooked through and drizzle with the lemon juice.
Spoon the mash onto a plate and lay the cod on top. No onion, no garlic.

title: Gluten-free porridge with strawberries and maple syrup
instructions: Simmer the gluten-free oats with the almond drink for 8 minutes into a creamy porridge, then take off the heat.
Slice the strawberries.
Spoon the porridge into a bowl, top with the strawberries and drizzle with 15 g maple syrup.

title: Turkey breast with roasted pumpkin, spinach and rice
instructions: Simmer the jasmine rice in 135 ml water for 15 minutes. Cut the pumpkin into 2 cm cubes, toss with 4 g rapeseed oil and roast at 200 °C for 20 minutes.
Fry the turkey breast in 4 g rapeseed oil for 6 minutes per side until cooked through, then deglaze with the lemon juice.
Wilt the spinach for 2 minutes.
Arrange the rice, pumpkin, spinach and turkey. No onion, no garlic.

title: Rice cakes with peanut butter, kiwi and hemp seeds
instructions: Peel the kiwi and cut it into slices.
Spread the rice cakes with 28 g peanut butter.
Lay the kiwi on top, scatter with 15 g hemp seeds and eat immediately.

title: Prawns with pak choi, ginger and jasmine rice
instructions: Simmer the jasmine rice in 150 ml water for 15 minutes. Halve the pak choi lengthways, finely grate the ginger and slice the spring onion greens into rings.
Fry the prawns in 8 g rapeseed oil for 3 minutes per side until pink and cooked through, then lift out.
Fry the pak choi and ginger for 3 minutes, then add 15 ml soy sauce and the spring onion greens.
Return the prawns and serve with the rice. No onion whites, no garlic.

title: Sheet-pan steak with carrots, courgette and potatoes
instructions: Quarter the potatoes, cut the carrot into batons and the courgette into thick slices. Toss with 4 g rapeseed oil, rosemary and thyme.
Roast the vegetables in the oven at 200 °C for 20 minutes.
Fry the steak in 4 g rapeseed oil in a pan for 3 minutes per side, then place it on the tray with the vegetables for 5 minutes in the oven to rest and finish.
Slice the steak, spread with 8 g mustard, drizzle with 8 ml lemon juice and serve with the lamb's lettuce and cucumber. No onion, no garlic.

title: Lactose-free vanilla berry ice cream with lime
instructions: Wash the strawberries and blueberries, blend 80 g of the berries until smooth and leave the rest whole.
Stir the lactose-free quark with the vanilla, lime juice, 10 g maple syrup and the berry puree until smooth, then fold in the whole berries.
Pour into a shallow tub and freeze for 3 hours, stirring vigorously every hour.
Leave to soften for 5 minutes before serving and shape 2 scoops.

title: Kiwi and banana rice-cake breakfast with peanut butter and lime
instructions: Slice the kiwi and the firm, slightly green banana.
Spread the rice cakes with 25 g peanut butter.
Lay the kiwi and banana on top, drizzle with 5 ml lime juice and eat immediately.

title: Oven salmon with courgette, carrots and rice
instructions: Simmer the basmati rice in 135 ml water for 15 minutes. Cut the courgette into slices and the carrot into slices.
Toss the vegetables with 4 g rapeseed oil and the dill, spread on a tray and place the salmon fillet on top with 4 g rapeseed oil and the lemon juice.
Bake at 200 °C for 15 minutes until the salmon is matte and tender. No onion, no garlic.

title: Trout on spelt with peas, carrots and herb yoghurt
instructions: Simmer the spelt in 110 ml water for 30 minutes until soft, then drain.
Slice the carrot and cook with the peas for 6 minutes.
Fry the trout in 8 g rapeseed oil for 4 minutes per side until cooked through. Stir the yoghurt with the parsley and dill.
Arrange the spelt, vegetables and trout and serve with the herb yoghurt.

title: Millet yoghurt cup with apple, pear and sunflower seeds
instructions: Simmer the millet in 120 ml water for 15 minutes, then cool.
Cut the apple and pear into small cubes. Toast the sunflower seeds in a pan for 2 minutes.
Layer the cold millet with the yoghurt, fruit cubes and seeds in a glass.

title: Turkey vegetable skewers with quinoa and tomato-cucumber salad
instructions: Simmer the quinoa in 120 ml water for 15 minutes. Cut the turkey breast, pepper and courgette into 3 cm pieces and thread them alternately onto 3 skewers.
Brush the skewers with 8 g rapeseed oil and cook in a grill pan for 8 minutes, turning often, until the turkey is cooked through.
Dice the tomato and cucumber and toss with the parsley into a salad.
Serve the skewers with the quinoa and salad.

title: Bean and corn skillet with egg, coriander and a corn tortilla
instructions: Dice the pepper and tomato. Drain the kidney beans and the corn.
Fry the pepper, beans, corn and tomato in 6 g rapeseed oil for 6 minutes. Crack the eggs on top and let them set for 3 minutes.
Warm the corn tortilla in a dry pan for 30 seconds per side.
Finish the skillet with coriander and lime juice and serve with the tortilla.

title: Courgette boats with turkey-tomato filling and a large salad
instructions: Halve the courgettes lengthways, hollow them out and finely chop the flesh.
Dice the turkey breast and tomato, fry with the courgette flesh and 5 g rapeseed oil for 6 minutes, then fold in the parsley.
Fill the courgette boats and bake at 190 °C for 15 minutes.
Serve with the large green salad and the yoghurt as a dip.

title: Tomato, cucumber and lentil bowl with herbs and yoghurt
instructions: Simmer the lentils in 125 ml water for 20 minutes until tender-crisp, then drain and cool.
Dice the tomato and cucumber and chop the parsley and mint.
Toss the lentils, tomato, cucumber and herbs with the lemon juice.
Spoon into a bowl and top with the yoghurt.

title: Turkey and fennel stew with green spelt and parsley
instructions: Simmer the green spelt in 75 ml water for 20 minutes. Cut the fennel into wedges and the turkey breast into cubes.
Fry the turkey in 6 g rapeseed oil for 5 minutes, add the fennel and stew together for 5 minutes.
Pour in 200 ml vegetable stock, simmer for 10 minutes, then fold in the green spelt and parsley.
Serve hot as a stew.

title: Large salad bowl with cottage cheese, chickpeas, cucumber and radishes
instructions: Slice the cucumber, thinly slice the radishes and tear the lettuce.
Drain the chickpeas.
Toss the lettuce, cucumber, radishes and chickpeas with the lemon juice and spoon the cottage cheese in the centre.

title: Roasted pumpkin breakfast bowl with yoghurt, granola and seeds
instructions: Cut the pumpkin into 2 cm cubes, toss with the cinnamon and roast at 200 °C for 20 minutes until soft.
Toast the oats and flaxseed in a non-stick pan for 3 minutes until golden; this is the granola.
Put the roasted pumpkin in a bowl and top with the yoghurt, granola and pumpkin seeds.

title: Stuffed pointed peppers with chicken, tomato and plenty of lettuce
instructions: Halve the pointed peppers lengthways and remove the seeds. Dice the chicken breast and tomato.
Fry the chicken in 5 g rapeseed oil for 6 minutes, then fold in the tomato and parsley.
Fill the pepper halves and bake at 190 °C for 15 minutes.
Serve with the large green salad.

title: Fennel and tomato stew with white beans and herbs
instructions: Cut the fennel into wedges and dice the tomato.
Fry the fennel in 5 g rapeseed oil for 5 minutes, then add the tomato, white beans and 150 ml vegetable stock.
Simmer for 12 minutes until the fennel is soft, then fold in the parsley and thyme.
Serve hot as a stew.

title: Roasted vegetable bowl with chickpeas, herb yoghurt and quinoa
instructions: Simmer the quinoa in 105 ml water for 15 minutes. Cut the pepper, courgette and carrot into wedges, toss with 8 g rapeseed oil and roast at 200 °C for 20 minutes.
Add the chickpeas to the tray with the vegetables for the last 5 minutes.
Stir the yoghurt with the parsley into a herb yoghurt.
Spoon the quinoa, roasted vegetables and chickpeas into a bowl and top with the herb yoghurt.

title: Braised rabbit with root vegetables and herbs
instructions: Cut the rabbit into 4 cm pieces and the carrot, parsnip and celeriac into large chunks.
Brown the meat in 10 g olive oil for 5 minutes on all sides, then lift out.
Fry the root vegetables for 5 minutes, return the rabbit, thyme and rosemary, add 1 tbsp water and braise covered for 30 minutes until the meat is tender.
Serve hot with the herbs. No potato, no cream, no flour.

title: Quail breast with grapes, Brussels sprouts and walnuts
instructions: Halve the Brussels sprouts, halve the grapes and roughly chop the walnuts.
Fry the quail breast in 4 g olive oil for 3 minutes per side until just cooked and still slightly pink, then lift out and rest for 3 minutes.
Fry the Brussels sprouts in 4 g olive oil for 8 minutes, add the grapes and walnuts for the last 3 minutes and scatter with thyme.
Slice the quail breast and serve on the vegetables.

title: Venison goulash with cranberries, parsnips and red cabbage
instructions: Cut the venison into 3 cm cubes, the parsnip into chunks and the red cabbage into strips.
Brown the meat in 8 g olive oil for 5 minutes on all sides, then lift out.
Fry the parsnip and red cabbage for 5 minutes, return the venison, thyme, juniper and 30 g unsweetened cranberries and braise covered for 30 minutes.
Serve hot. No flour, no cream, no potato.

title: Duck leg with braised chicory and orange
instructions: Pat the duck leg dry, quarter the chicory lengthways, segment the orange and keep the juice.
Start the duck leg skin-side down in a cold pan with no extra fat, fry for 8 minutes until the skin is crisp, turn, fry for 4 minutes and lift out.
Fry the chicory in 5 g olive oil in the same pan for 5 minutes, pour in the orange juice and braise for 10 minutes.
Place the duck leg on the chicory and finish in the oven at 180 °C for 15 minutes, adding the orange segments for the last 3 minutes.

title: Venison loin with buttered Brussels sprouts and cranberries
instructions: Halve the Brussels sprouts. Pat the venison loin dry.
Fry the loin in 10 g butter for 3 minutes per side, then lift out and rest for 5 minutes.
Fry the Brussels sprouts in the remaining 40 g butter for 8 minutes until golden, adding 15 g unsweetened cranberries and the thyme in the last minute.
Slice the venison and serve on the buttered Brussels sprouts with the cranberries.

title: Hemp coconut pudding with raspberries and toasted coconut chips
instructions: Blend the hemp seeds with the coconut milk for 1 minute until very fine and a creamy pudding forms. Chill for 2 hours.
Toast the coconut flakes in a non-stick pan for 2 minutes until golden.
Spoon the pudding into a bowl and top with 40 g raspberries and the toasted coconut chips.

title: Cauliflower risotto with prawns and parmesan
instructions: Grate or chop the cauliflower into very fine rice-sized grains. Pat the prawns dry and finely grate the parmesan.
Fry the prawns in 10 g olive oil for 2 minutes per side until pink, then lift out.
Stew the cauliflower in 22 g butter and the remaining olive oil for 6 minutes until tender but not mushy, then stir in the parmesan and parsley.
Arrange the prawns on the cauliflower risotto. No rice, no cream.

title: Olive and almond cream on cucumber slices
instructions: Stone the olives. Cut the cucumber into 1 cm-thick slices.
Blend the olives, almonds, 15 g olive oil and the lemon juice into a coarse, spreadable cream.
Spoon the cream onto the cucumber slices and eat immediately.

title: Ricotta coffee mousse with cacao nibs
instructions: Beat the ricotta and mascarpone with the cooled espresso for 1 minute until creamy.
Spoon the mousse into a bowl and chill for 30 minutes.
Scatter with 10 g cacao nibs and serve.

title: Scrambled eggs with chanterelles, parsley and chives
instructions: Clean the chanterelles and halve any large ones. Chop the parsley and chives. Beat the eggs.
Fry the chanterelles in 8 g butter for 5 minutes until they have some colour.
Add the eggs and let them set creamily for 2 minutes, then fold in the herbs and 5 ml lemon juice.
Slice the radishes and serve with the scrambled eggs as breakfast.

title: Turkey breast with sage lemon butter and fried courgette
instructions: Cut the courgette into 1 cm-thick slices and pick the sage leaves.
Fry the turkey breast in 5 g butter for 6 minutes per side until cooked through, then lift out and rest for 3 minutes.
Fry the courgette in the remaining 10 g butter for 4 minutes per side, adding the sage and lemon juice in the last minute.
Slice the turkey and serve with the courgette and the sage lemon butter.

title: Air-fryer cheese balls with pepper salad
instructions: Finely grate the light cheese, knead with the egg and almond flour into a dough and shape 8 small balls.
Brush the balls with 5 g rapeseed oil and bake in the air fryer at 180 °C for 10 minutes until golden.
Cut the pepper and lettuce into strips.
Serve the cheese balls with the pepper salad as a snack.

title: Pike-perch fillet on leaf spinach with almond butter
instructions: Pat the pike-perch fillet dry. Wash the spinach.
Fry the pike-perch in a non-stick pan for 4 minutes per side until cooked through, deglaze with the lemon juice and lift out.
Wilt the spinach in the same pan for 2 minutes, then stir in 20 g almond butter until a glossy sauce forms.
Arrange the spinach and lay the pike-perch on top.

title: Warm quinoa bowl with roasted quince, cinnamon and skyr
instructions: Simmer the quinoa in 120 ml water for 15 minutes. Peel and core the quince and cut it into wedges.
Toss the quince wedges with 5 g rapeseed oil and the cinnamon and roast at 200 °C for 20 minutes until soft.
Spoon the warm quinoa into a bowl and top with the roasted quince and the skyr.

title: Beetroot pancakes with goat's cheese and dill
instructions: Finely grate the beetroot. Stir in the oats and egg white and leave to swell for 5 minutes.
In 3 g rapeseed oil in a non-stick pan, cook 3 thin pancakes for 3 minutes per side.
Crumble the goat's cheese. Have the lamb's lettuce and dill ready.
Serve the pancakes with 10 g goat's cheese, the lamb's lettuce and the dill as breakfast.

title: Cinnamon orange porridge with pistachios
instructions: Simmer the oats with the oat drink and cinnamon for 8 minutes into a creamy porridge.
Segment the orange and roughly chop the pistachios.
Spoon the porridge into a bowl and top with the orange segments and pistachios.

title: Roasted chestnuts with rosemary and apple wedges
instructions: If needed, score the chestnuts. Core the apple and cut it into wedges.
Toss the chestnuts and apple wedges with 6 g olive oil, rosemary and 0.2 g sea salt.
Roast in the oven at 200 °C for 20 minutes until the chestnuts are soft and the apple wedges are lightly browned.
Serve warm as a snack.

title: Green asparagus with salmon, dill yoghurt and boiled potatoes
instructions: Peel the potatoes and boil them in salted water for 15 minutes until tender, then drain. Peel the lower third of the asparagus.
Fry the asparagus in 3 g rapeseed oil for 6 minutes until tender-crisp and bright green.
Fry the salmon in 3 g rapeseed oil for 4 minutes per side until just cooked and matte, then drizzle with 8 ml lemon juice. Stir the yoghurt with the dill.
Arrange the potatoes, asparagus, salmon and rocket and serve with the dill yoghurt.

title: Wild garlic risotto with green asparagus and lemon zest
instructions: Peel the lower third of the asparagus and cut it into 3 cm pieces. Roughly chop the wild garlic, finely grate the hard cheese and zest the lemon.
Sweat the round-grain rice in 8 g olive oil for 1 minute, pour in 160 ml hot vegetable stock and simmer for 18 minutes, stirring, adding the asparagus for the last 6 minutes.
Fold in the wild garlic, hard cheese and lemon zest and serve immediately.

title: Rhubarb crumble with oat streusel and skyr
instructions: Cut the rhubarb into 2 cm pieces, put it into a small ovenproof dish and mix with the cinnamon.
Rub the oats with 5 g rapeseed oil into a streusel and scatter over the rhubarb.
Bake at 180 °C for 20 minutes until the streusel is golden and the rhubarb is juicy.
Cool for 5 minutes and serve with the skyr.

title: Chestnut and savoy cabbage skillet with turkey and potatoes
instructions: Cut the potatoes into 1.5 cm cubes, the savoy cabbage into strips, the turkey breast into strips and the onion into wedges.
Fry the potatoes in 4 g rapeseed oil for 10 minutes until golden. Add the turkey and onion and fry for 6 minutes.
Add the savoy cabbage and chestnuts, stew with 4 g rapeseed oil for 6 minutes until the cabbage has wilted.
Serve hot as a skillet.

title: Savoy cabbage lasagne with ricotta, nutmeg and tomato sauce
instructions: Separate the savoy cabbage into large leaves, blanch for 3 minutes and drain. Simmer the passata with 6 g olive oil and the nutmeg for 5 minutes.

Spread a little tomato sauce in a small dish, layer alternately cabbage, ricotta and wholemeal lasagne sheets, finishing with sauce. Spread 50 g lasagne sheets, 40 g ricotta and 200 g savoy cabbage evenly.
Bake at 180 °C for 25 minutes until the top is bubbling and the sheets are soft. Rest for 5 minutes.
Serve one piece as a main. No large block of parmesan on top.

title: Kale and potato skillet with egg and mustard yoghurt
instructions: Cut the potatoes into 1 cm cubes and the kale into large pieces. Stir the yoghurt with 8 g mustard.
Fry the potatoes in 3 g rapeseed oil for 10 minutes until golden. Add the kale and stew for 5 minutes.
Make a well, crack the eggs into it and let them set for 3 minutes.
Serve the skillet with the mustard yoghurt as breakfast.

title: Strapatsada (Greek tomato scrambled eggs with oregano) and wholemeal bread
instructions: Dice the tomatoes and simmer them in some of the olive oil for 8 minutes until soft and juicy.
Beat the egg and egg white, add to the tomatoes and gently scramble over medium heat for 3–4 minutes. Fold in the oregano and onion.
Fold in the spinach, season with chilli, sesame, salt and pepper and serve with the toasted slice of wholemeal bread.

title: Sfougato (Greek zucchini herb omelette with feta) and tomato cucumber salad
instructions: Coarsely grate the zucchini, leave with a pinch of salt for 5 minutes and squeeze out well.
Mix with the egg, egg white, crumbled feta, dill and mint. Cook in olive oil until golden on both sides.

Dice the tomatoes and cucumber, mix with capers and lemon juice and serve as a salad with the omelette. Fold the spinach into the omelette batter beforehand, and serve with a slice of wholemeal bread.

title: Ladenia (Cycladic olive-oil flatbread with tomato, onion and oregano)
instructions: Knead the wholemeal flour with the water, half the olive oil and a pinch of salt to a soft dough and rest for 15 minutes.
Press the dough flat onto a tray and top with tomato and onion slices.
Drizzle with the remaining oil and oregano and bake at 200 °C for 20 minutes until golden.

title: Uova in purgatorio (eggs in a spicy tomato sauce) with wholemeal bread
instructions: Sweat the onion and garlic in olive oil for 3 minutes, add the chilli and passata and simmer for 8 minutes.
Make wells in the sauce, slide in the egg and egg white and cover for 4 minutes until just set.
Season with basil, salt and pepper, top with rocket and serve with toasted wholemeal bread.

title: Taktouka with a fried egg, cumin and wholemeal bread
instructions: Dice the peppers and tomatoes and braise with the garlic in olive oil for 12 minutes until soft. Stir in the cumin and paprika.
Fry the egg in a small pan, leaving the yolk soft.
Stew the soft zucchini with the peppers in the last minutes. Plate the taktouka with herbs, lemon juice, sesame and the fried egg, and serve the wholemeal bread alongside.

title: Huevos a la flamenca with peas, peppers and wholemeal bread
instructions: Sweat the pepper, onion, carrot and garlic in olive oil for 5 minutes, add the tomatoes and peas and braise for 8 minutes.
Make wells in the vegetables, slide in the eggs and cover for 4–5 minutes until just set.
Season with parsley and the spices and serve with toasted wholemeal bread.

title: Ervilhas com ovos (Portuguese peas with a poached egg and coriander)
instructions: Sweat the onion in olive oil for 3 minutes, add the peas and tomatoes and cook gently for 8 minutes.
Poach the egg in barely simmering water for 3 minutes and drain.
Season the peas with lemon juice, coriander and the spices, fold in diced cucumber and top with the poached egg.

title: Frisella pugliese with tomato, rocket, oregano and olive oil
instructions: Briefly moisten the wholemeal frisella with a little water so it softens without turning soggy.
Dice the tomatoes and mix with olive oil, oregano, olives, salt and pepper.
Add diced cucumber, capers and vinegar to the tomato mixture, spoon it onto the frisella and top with the rocket.

title: Farinata di ceci with rosemary, red onions and a rocket salad
instructions: Whisk the chickpea flour with the water until smooth, rest 10 minutes, then stir in olive oil, rosemary, salt and pepper.
Pour into a hot, lightly oiled pan, top with onion slices and bake at 220 °C for 15 minutes until golden.
Cut into wedges and serve with the rocket salad.

title: Kalitsounia (Cretan herb and cheese pastries) with tomato salad
instructions: Knead the wholemeal flour with the water and some of the olive oil to a dough and rest for 10 minutes.
Mash the feta with mint and dill. Roll the dough into circles, fill and pinch closed.
Fry in the remaining oil for 3–4 minutes per side until golden, or bake at 200 °C for 15 minutes. Serve with the tomato and cucumber salad.

title: Poached eggs on peperonata with wholemeal bread
instructions: Braise the peppers, fennel and onion in olive oil for 10 minutes until soft, add the tomatoes, capers and basil and cook 5 minutes more.
Poach the egg and egg white in barely simmering water for 3–4 minutes.
Spoon the peperonata onto the plate, top with the poached egg and rocket and serve with toasted wholemeal bread.

title: Broad-bean breakfast pan with dill, lemon and a poached egg
instructions: Warm the broad beans with the spring onion and diced carrot in olive oil for 5 minutes, add the diced tomatoes and braise for 4 minutes.
Season with dill, lemon juice and the spices.
Poach the egg for 3 minutes, set it on the pan and serve at once.

title: White-bean shakshuka with chard and cumin
instructions: Sweat the onion and garlic in olive oil, then simmer the passata, cumin and paprika for 6 minutes.
Stir in the white beans and chopped chard and cook for 5 minutes until the chard wilts.
Make a well, slide in the egg, cover for 4 minutes until set. Serve with parsley.

title: Wholemeal crostini with white-bean cream, rosemary and roasted tomatoes
instructions: Roast the tomatoes with a little olive oil, salt and pepper at 200 °C for 15 minutes.
Blend the white beans with rosemary, garlic, lemon juice and the remaining oil to a cream.
Toast the wholemeal bread, spread with the cream and top with the roasted tomatoes, capers, a little feta, sesame and chilli. Serve with lamb's lettuce, rocket and orange segments beside.

title: Savoury yoghurt breakfast with spelt rusks, tomato, olive and oregano
instructions: Spoon the yoghurt into a bowl and stir until smooth.
Dice the tomatoes and mix with the olives, oregano and olive oil, season with salt and pepper.
Spoon the mixture with cucumber, radishes, rocket and lamb's lettuce over the yoghurt and serve with the crunchy spelt rusks.

title: Melon with ricotta, mint and toasted pistachios
instructions: Cut the honeydew melon into wedges and arrange on a plate.
Add the ricotta in the centre or in small spoonfuls and drizzle with olive oil.
Scatter over the chopped mint and toasted pistachios and serve at once.

title: Blood-orange yoghurt with olive oil, pistachio and thyme
instructions: Segment the blood oranges, catching the juice.
Spoon the yoghurt into a bowl, stir in the orange juice and top with the segments.
Finish with olive oil, roughly chopped pistachios and thyme.

title: Scrambled eggs with green asparagus, pecorino and wholemeal bread
instructions: Cut the asparagus into pieces and sauté in olive oil for 4 minutes until just tender.
Beat the egg and egg white, add to the asparagus and gently scramble over low heat for 2–3 minutes.
Scatter over the pecorino, parsley, radish slices and diced tomato and serve with toasted wholemeal bread.

title: Mint and feta omelette with fresh tomatoes and olives
instructions: Beat the egg and egg white with chopped mint, set as an omelette in olive oil, scatter in the feta and fold.
Dice the tomatoes and mix with the olives.
Serve the omelette with the tomato salad, rocket, radishes and toasted wholemeal bread.

title: Arroz de tomate com ovo (Portuguese tomato rice with egg and coriander)
instructions: Sweat the onion and garlic in olive oil, then briefly toast the brown rice with them.
Add the passata and 130 ml water and simmer for 20 minutes until the rice is tender.
Fold the peas into the rice in the last minutes. Fry the egg in a pan or crack it onto the rice and let it just set. Serve with coriander and a little chilli.

title: Revuelto de trigueros (scrambled eggs with wild asparagus and pepper)
instructions: Sauté the asparagus and pepper in olive oil for 5 minutes.
Add the beaten egg and egg white and gently scramble for 2–3 minutes until just set.
Season with parsley, salt and pepper and serve with wholemeal bread.

title: Myzithra plate with cucumber, tomato, olive and olive oil
instructions: Place the myzithra in spoonfuls in the centre of the plate.
Cut the cucumber and tomato into pieces and mix with olives, oregano, mint and olive oil.
Arrange the vegetables with lamb's lettuce, rocket, capers, chilli, lemon juice and pomegranate seeds around the cheese and serve with toasted wholemeal bread.

title: Baked ricotta slices with zucchini, mint and lemon zest
instructions: Mix the ricotta with mint, lemon zest and a little salt and shape into a flat slab.
Slice the zucchini, spread on a tray with olive oil and add the ricotta slab.
Bake at 200 °C for 15 minutes until the edges are golden. Serve with lemon juice and wholemeal bread.

title: Revuelto de garbanzos (scrambled eggs with chickpeas, coriander and tomato)
instructions: Sweat the onion in olive oil, then sauté the chickpeas and diced tomatoes with it for 4 minutes.
Beat the egg and egg white, fold through and let set for 2 minutes.
Fold in the pepper and diced cucumber, season with coriander, salt and pepper and serve at once.

title: Focaccia breakfast with roasted peppers, rocket and a soft egg
instructions: Knead the wholemeal flour with the water, some of the oil, rosemary and oregano, press flat on a tray and rest 10 minutes.
Pre-bake at 220 °C for 12 minutes, then drizzle with the remaining oil.
Cook the egg soft or fry it. Top the focaccia with roasted peppers, rocket and the egg.

title: Balila breakfast (warm chickpeas with cumin, lemon, parsley and egg)
instructions: Warm the chickpeas with a ladle of their cooking liquid or a little water, cumin and olive oil for 5 minutes, lightly crushing some of them.
Season with lemon juice, parsley and spring onion, and fold in the diced tomatoes.
Fold in diced cucumber and radish. Fry or poach the egg and set it on the warm chickpeas.

title: Baked eggs in a chard nest with cherry tomatoes and olive oil
instructions: Wilt the chard with garlic in olive oil for 4 minutes and arrange as a nest in a small baking dish.
Add the cherry tomatoes and slide the egg and egg white into the centre.
Bake at 190 °C for 8–10 minutes until the white is set. Serve with toasted wholemeal bread.

title: Wholemeal pitta pockets with rocket, white cheese, cucumber and oregano
instructions: Warm the wholemeal pitta briefly in a toaster or pan and split it open.
Crumble the feta and mix with oregano and olive oil.
Fill the pitta with rocket, cucumber, radishes, tomato and the feta mixture and eat at once.

title: Fasolada (Greek white bean soup with celery, carrot and olive oil)
instructions: Sweat the onion, carrot and celery in olive oil for 6 minutes.
Add the white beans, passata and the low-sodium stock and simmer gently for 20 minutes.
Season with parsley and the spices and serve with a drizzle of olive oil.

title: Fasolakia ladera (Greek green beans and potatoes in tomato and olive oil)
instructions: Sweat the onion and garlic in olive oil, then simmer the passata with them for 3 minutes.
Add the green beans and diced potatoes, pour in a little water and braise covered for 25 minutes.
Season with dill, parsley and lemon juice and serve with a slice of wholemeal bread.

title: Fakes soupa (Greek lentil soup with red wine vinegar and olive oil)
instructions: Sweat the onion, carrot and celeriac in olive oil for 5 minutes, then briefly toast the lentils with them.
Add the passata and stock and simmer for 25 minutes until the lentils are soft.
Season with red wine vinegar, lemon juice, oregano and parsley and finish with olive oil. Serve with lamb's lettuce, grapefruit pieces and a slice of wholemeal bread.

title: Hortopita (Greek wild-herb pie with olive oil and feta)
instructions: Wilt the spinach and chard with the onion in a pan, squeeze well and mix with feta, dill and mint.
Roll out the wholemeal dough made from flour, water and some of the oil, and line a dish with half of it.
Add the filling, cover with the remaining dough, brush with the rest of the oil and bake at 200 °C for 25 minutes until golden.

title: Kolokithokeftedes (Greek zucchini and feta fritters) with tzatziki and tomato salad
instructions: Grate and squeeze the zucchini and mix with feta, flour, egg, dill and mint to a batter.
Fry small fritters in a little olive oil for 3 minutes per side until golden.
Stir the yoghurt with cucumber and garlic into tzatziki and serve with tomato salad, rocket and a slice of wholemeal bread.

title: Revithokeftedes (Greek chickpea patties) with cabbage salad and lemon
instructions: Coarsely mash the chickpeas with onion, herbs and flour and shape into small patties.
Fry in olive oil for 3–4 minutes per side until golden.
Finely shred the cabbage and carrot, dress with lemon juice and serve with the patties.

title: Spanakorizo (Greek spinach rice with dill, lemon and feta)
instructions: Sweat the onion in olive oil and briefly toast the brown rice with it.
Add 130 ml water, simmer 15 minutes, fold in the spinach and dill and cook 5 minutes more.
Season with lemon juice and crumble the feta on top.

title: Prasorizo (Greek leek rice with dill, olive oil and yoghurt)
instructions: Sweat the leeks in olive oil for 6 minutes until soft, add the brown rice and cook briefly.
Add 130 ml water and simmer for 20 minutes until the rice is tender. Fold in the dill.
Season with lemon juice and serve with the yoghurt.

title: Lachanorizo (Greek cabbage rice with tomato, dill and olive oil)
instructions: Sweat the onion in olive oil, then sweat the cabbage with it for 5 minutes.
Add the brown rice and passata, pour in 130 ml water and simmer for 20 minutes.
Fold in the dill, finish with a spoon of yoghurt and serve hot.

title: Trahana soup with tomato, feta and mint
instructions: Warm the olive oil in a pot, stir in the trahana, then add the passata and stock.
Simmer for 15 minutes until the trahana is soft and the soup is creamy.
Add the mint and feta and serve with a slice of wholemeal bread.

title: Tirokafteri (spicy feta and pepper dip) with vegetable sticks and wholemeal pitta
instructions: Blend the feta, roasted peppers, yoghurt, chilli and olive oil to a creamy but still slightly chunky dip.
Season with oregano, salt and pepper.
Serve with carrot and cucumber sticks and warm wholemeal pitta.

title: Melitzanosalata with pomegranate, parsley and wholemeal pitta
instructions: Slash the aubergine and roast at 220 °C for 25 minutes until soft and smoky, then scoop out the flesh.
Coarsely mash with garlic, olive oil, lemon juice and parsley.
Fold in diced cucumber and sesame, scatter with pomegranate seeds and serve with toasted wholemeal bread.

title: Lahanodolmades (cabbage rolls with herb rice and egg-lemon sauce)
instructions: Blanch the cabbage leaves. Mix the rice with the herbs, onion and some of the oil and roll in the leaves.
Steam the rolls in a pot with the stock, covered, for 25 minutes.
Beat the egg with lemon juice, whisk in a little hot stock and pour the sauce over the rolls.

title: Papoutsakia (stuffed aubergines with lentils, tomato and yoghurt)
instructions: Halve the aubergines lengthways, hollow them out and pre-bake the shells at 200 °C for 10 minutes.
Braise the lentils with onion, garlic, passata and the chopped aubergine flesh for 15 minutes.
Fill the shells, bake 15 minutes more and serve with yoghurt, lemon juice and parsley.

title: Maftoul with chicken, chickpeas and pumpkin
instructions: Brown the chicken in olive oil with the onion and spices for 6 minutes.
Add the pumpkin and chickpeas, pour in a little water and braise for 12 minutes.
Cook the maftoul separately for 12 minutes and plate with the stew and herbs.

title: Shish tawook with bulgur salad and garlic yoghurt dip
instructions: Marinate the chicken in yoghurt, garlic, lemon juice and some of the oil, thread onto skewers and grill or pan-fry for 10–12 minutes.
Soak the bulgur in hot water for 12 minutes and mix with cucumber, tomato and herbs.
Stir the remaining garlic into the rest of the yoghurt and serve as a dip with the skewers and salad.

title: Mujaddara (lentil rice with fried onions, cucumber yoghurt and cabbage salad)
instructions: Fry half the onion in olive oil until deep golden and set aside.
Cook the lentils and brown rice with the remaining onion and cumin in water for 25 minutes.
Top with the fried onions and serve with cucumber yoghurt and cabbage salad dressed with lemon.

title: Loubieh b zeit (Lebanese green beans in tomato and olive oil) with bulgur
instructions: Sweat the onion and garlic in olive oil, then simmer the passata for 3 minutes.
Add the green beans and braise covered for 20 minutes until tender.
Cook the bulgur in 100 ml water for 12 minutes and serve with parsley, chilli, sesame, diced cucumber, lemon juice and pomegranate seeds alongside the beans.

title: Maghmour (Lebanese aubergine and chickpea moussaka)
instructions: Fry the aubergine cubes in olive oil for 8 minutes until golden, then add the onion and garlic.
Add the passata, chickpeas and mint and braise for 15 minutes.
Season with lemon juice and pomegranate seeds and serve warm or at room temperature.

title: Hindbeh b zeit (braised cicoria with fried onions, olive oil and wholemeal flatbread)
instructions: Blanch the cicoria in salted water for 5 minutes, squeeze well and chop roughly.
Fry the onion in olive oil until golden, add the greens and toss for 5 minutes.
Season with lemon juice and serve with the warm wholemeal flatbread.

title: Zaalouk (Moroccan aubergine and tomato mash with cumin) and wholemeal bread
instructions: Dice the aubergine and tomatoes and braise with garlic in olive oil for 15 minutes until soft.
Mash with a spoon and stir in cumin, paprika and lemon juice.
Fold in the chickpeas and shaved fennel, scatter with chilli, capers, sesame, pomegranate seeds, coriander and parsley, and serve with rocket, yoghurt and wholemeal bread.

title: Bissara (Moroccan broad-bean soup with cumin and olive oil)
instructions: Simmer the broad beans with garlic, cumin, the tomatoes and the stock for 10 minutes and blend until smooth.
Season with lemon juice and paprika and stir in the olive oil.
Blend the carrot and pepper with the beans and serve with chilli, sesame, parsley and a slice of wholemeal bread.

title: Tabbouleh (Lebanese parsley and bulgur salad with tomato and mint)
instructions: Soak the bulgur in a little hot water for 10 minutes and drain.
Chop the parsley and mint very finely, dice the tomatoes and spring onion.
Toss everything with olive oil and lemon juice and serve with warm wholemeal pitta.

title: Raheb salad (smoky aubergine salad with tomato, pepper and pomegranate)
instructions: Roast the aubergine at 220 °C for 25 minutes until smoky and dice the flesh.
Mix with tomato, pepper, spring onion, parsley, olive oil and lemon juice.
Fold in diced cucumber and sesame, scatter with pomegranate seeds and serve with wholemeal pitta.

title: Fregola sarda with mussels, saffron, tomato and parsley
instructions: Sweat the onion and garlic in olive oil, toast the fregola briefly, then add the passata and saffron.
Simmer with 150 ml water for 12 minutes, add the mussels and cook 6 minutes more until just cooked.
Finish with parsley and serve hot.

title: Malloreddus with saffron tomato sauce, peas and pecorino
instructions: Cook the wholemeal malloreddus in salted water until al dente, adding the peas for the last 2 minutes.
Sweat the onion in olive oil and simmer the passata and saffron for 8 minutes.
Toss the pasta and peas in the sauce and serve with pecorino and basil.

title: Fagioli all'uccelletto (Tuscan beans in tomato and sage) with wholemeal bread
instructions: Warm the garlic and sage in olive oil for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Add the passata and white beans and simmer for 15 minutes.
Fold in the fennel pieces and chilli, season and serve with toasted wholemeal bread.

title: Vignarola (Roman spring vegetables with artichokes, peas and broad beans)
instructions: Sweat the spring onion in olive oil for 3 minutes, add the artichoke hearts and cook 5 minutes more.
Add the peas, broad beans and stock and braise for 10 minutes.
Season with mint, parsley and lemon juice and serve just warm.

title: Pomodori al riso (Roman baked tomatoes with herb rice and potatoes)
instructions: Slice the tops off the tomatoes, hollow them out and mix the insides with brown rice, herbs, garlic and some of the oil.
